findings.title: Overload inner entry does not check its actual50ms-limited deadline
findings.detail: The effective overload_deadline is min(accepted2s deadline,now+original50ms), but inner future only compares std now to the accepted2s deadline. If first poll occurs after50ms but before2s, inner can start write_all even though its actual overload deadline expired. Tokio timeout is not an entry admission barrier.

local_pinned_source_evidence.observation: Timeout<T>::poll tries me.value.poll first, only then polls deadline. This is local matching-version source inspection, not a new test or complete official crate integrity audit.

findings.required_narrow_change: Compare tokio::time::Instant::now() directly to the already computed overload_deadline at inner future entry. Keep min2s/50ms and original values; do not rely only on timeout_at or extend windows.
findings.not_runtime_failure: Static counter-schedule from existing poll order; no native/compiler failure was observed in this review.

preserved_source_semantics: Accepted actual stream deadline is created once before peer validation and reused for the original execution object; no new deadline after queuing.

Existing stream.ensure_current_user_peer is called immediately after accept before semaphore acquisition, overload protocol write, spawn or request reads. Err/expiredcontinue drops that actual stream naturally; no response or permit on refusal.
Original peer producer is unchanged: supported Unix uses actual OS peer UID; Windows remains Unsupported and therefore connections refuse rather than fabricating PID/SID proof.

Existing execution.check is called at spawned task start before serve_connection future; original cancellation drop guard and permit remain retained on the original task. Timeout is used for cleanup, not issuance of peer or execution authority.
No schema/request handler/serve suffix, wire frame cap,32semaphore size,2swindow or50msoverload constant changes. Original68tests/consumer APIs/providers/nativepeer/pathDACL are not replaced.
limits: Fixing first-poll entry is narrower than proving every later write_all poll or physical cleanup finishes within50ms. The existing timeout future polls its body first on later polls too; no whole-I/O hard latency bound is qualified. If per-poll no-expired-bytes is required, it needs a separate reviewed deadline-aware I/O implementation.
Existing synchronous OS peer query is not preempted by deadline; code can refuse later protocol admission after it returns, not prove hard accepted-socket retirement latency.
Windows functional peer producer and private socket DACL are still open; adding fail-closed consumption does not qualify ordinary Windows control service.
No actual Agentd caller/package/native tests, fullCI, real model/host/SDK budget renewal or bf36 V8 build was run.
